title.label: Good but lots room for improvement

content.label: The app does what it’s supposed to. The program library is great. You’ll definitely find a program that will meet your goals whatever they are. And the exercise library is reasonably decent. The strength score is an excellent heuristic for general strength progression, however there’s no explanation for where that score is coming from and no means to adjust the formula to fit your specific goals. Certainly there are weighting factors assigned to different muscles, motion patterns, etc. Those weighting factors should be customizable to fit your specific goals, but the app basically decides for you what is being weighted and to what degree. Data logging is fine, but data visualization is lacking. Nothing more than simple line charts. That’s it. You can’t even export your logged data so that it can be manipulated elsewhere.

I’ve used many fitness trackers over the years and Caliber is, by far, my favorite. They make the UX so convenient and it’s obvious their developers have taken a ton of time to put flows together. Kudos to the Caliber team! I love it!

title.label: Caliber Helped Me Regain My Strength

content.label:
After dealing with shingles for two months last year, I was out of shape, drained, and hesitant to jump back into strength training. At 46, I had lost a good amount of weight but was feeling physically weak — and more importantly, unsure how to start again without risking injury. That’s when I found Caliber, and everything changed.

From the very beginning, Johnny, my coach, stood out as someone truly invested in my health. During our initial consultation, he listened intently — not just to my goals, but to my history, including old injuries that make certain exercises a challenge. He took everything I said seriously. I never once felt dismissed or rushed, which had been a constant frustration with other apps and trainers.

Johnny customized a program that was thoughtful, safe, and incredibly motivating. Every exercise felt purposeful. He gave detailed feedback, adjusted routines when something didn’t feel right, and pushed me just the right amount to rediscover my old strength — and then surpass it.

Over just three months, I experienced a level of progress I hadn’t thought possible. I’m lifting more than I ever imagined at this stage in life. Every week I felt stronger, more capable, and more confident in my body. It’s hard to describe how powerful that is when you’ve been feeling broken for a long time.

What sets Caliber apart is how seriously they take their coaching. It’s not a generic plan or a bot-generated routine. It’s real human coaching with professional-level care. Other training apps I’ve tried felt impersonal or gimmicky — Caliber is the real deal.

If you’re like me — older than your 20s, working through some injuries, and trying to regain control over your strength and health — Caliber (and especially Johnny) might be exactly what you need. This was hands down one of the best decisions I’ve made for my fitness in years.

Thank you, Johnny, and thank you, Caliber!

title.label: 10 month review from a 70 year old male

content.label:
I am 70 years old, healthy and active. The book “Outlive” makes a strong case for the value of weight training for folks my age. The goal is to live out as many more years as I can with vigor, with the ability to continue to thrive: physically and mentally. 

So after training mostly body-weight exercises for nearly a year I installed Caliber on my phone. I was at first impressed by the concept of “relative strength” and how the app would give you weekly ratings of it. So after 10 months of training here is my review:

I signed up with a coach, Cameron who set up a weight routine of four times a week. 

The best thing about Caliber is 1) the routine that Cameron set me up with is really good. 2) the ability to log my sets and reps and see a complete history of each exercise and to keep notes about how i feel with each exercise, 3) having someone to answer to, to ask questions, to review my execution of the exercises video, to adapt my routine to injuries, etc.  A face to face trainer is expensive. This is a great less expensive alternative. 

The relative strength thing has proven to be more confusing and discouraging than helpful. My body looks and feels stronger than it has in a very long time but the relative strength goes up when it seems it should go down and down when it seems it should go up. 

A trainer once wrote that one should judge his progressed based on the mirror rather than the scale. It seems he may have been on to something.

It’s really frustrating. I want to like it but the interface is just difficult. Every workout I have to go and manually enter the exercise and if I don’t know the specific wording that the app uses, the exercise doesn’t come up. I’m sitting on a machine right now trying to find rear delt fly. Delt fly. Deltoid fly, rear deltoid fly. None of it comes up. I know it’s in here, I’ve found it before but now I have to go back though old workouts to try and find it, and that’s a huge pain. The search function for exercises is horrible. I spend more time on the app than I do exercising. I don’t get why I can’t just build a workout I want, then pull that one up and log it, add to it, modify it as I go. It’s really confusing. The interface could be better.

I have tried so many workout apps and this is truly the best one that fits my needs. They have so many already loaded workouts that I haven’t needed to create any so I can’t give a review on that, but I did have their AI build me a workout and honestly it was pretty spot on. You can easily change things and fit it to your needs and the equipment or lack there of. It also auto tracks your workouts you log on Apple so I don’t have to go into the app and manually add it. 

Just like with anything they could improve some things like mass adding workouts to multiple days or setting it up to auto populate each week till you cancel it. 

But that’s honestly so minor in the grand scheme of things. 

Best workout app and I plan on pushing this out to all my friends.

I like caliber because it gives you a strength score and tracks your workouts. Caliber helped me start working out, and because of this it helped me gain a lot of progress and THAT is why I gave it a five star review 😀

I’ve been looking for a workout app that gives me other ideas on what to do at the gym for a long time and this is it so far.
